model_assumptions: Linear small-amplitude spin waves in a soft isotropic ferromagnetic thin film
In-plane equilibrium magnetization and applied field

variables.phi: angle of wave vector relative to the applied field

contour_parameterization_inference.validity: r>0 and 0<=C_r<=1 in the first quadrant
contour_parameterization_inference.status: Algebraic rearrangement of the published dispersion, not an additional empirical model.

higher_order_near_point.location: PDF pp.12-13, Section III.D and Fig.13
higher_order_near_point.important_limit: The authors explicitly state that the hand-refined Fig.13 parameters are close to, but not exactly at, the mathematical higher-order critical point. Their precise local caustic position is sensitive to eta.

ordinary_comparison_from_paper.location: Fig.13 inset and PDF p.13 text
ordinary_comparison_from_paper.source_result: A small frequency change restores a quadratic variation of apparent wavelength around the ordinary caustic.

scalar_demo_boundary: Use finite spectral support and explicitly normalize a common modal-power measure.
Hold propagation distance and damping fixed for comparison; do not renormalize output peaks individually.
A contour integral using this band tests coherent geometric focusing only.
Without the tensor susceptibility, realistic antenna field and material-specific normalization, it does not predict absolute magnetic amplitude or solve the complete experimental outlook.
